events.title: Music: The Sounds of Math, Science & Social Studies (Fall 2026)
events.description:
[vc_row][vc_column][vc_column_text css=””]Registration closes Friday 10/9 at 12:00PM. 

Course Title: Music: The Sounds of Math, Science & Social Studies

Dates:
Session 1 — Saturday, October 10th. 9:00 – 5:00 (In-Person)
Session 2 — Saturday, October 17th. 9:00 – 5:00 (In-Person)
Session 3 — Saturday, October 24th. 9:00 – 5:00 (In-Person)
Session 4 — Thursday, October 29th. 4:00 – 7:00 (Virtual)
Session 5 — Saturday, October 31st. 9:00 – 5:00 (Virtual)
Session 6 — Thursday, November 5th. 4:00 – 7:30 (Virtual)
Session 7 — Saturday, November 7th. 9:00 – 5:00 (Virtual)

Credits: 3 P-Credit/45 CTLE hours*
Fee: $240 (MFTA*)+ $125 (ASPDP)

Course Description: This course is designed for teachers to integrate music into the classroom through fun and simple techniques. Build instruments from upcycled materials, drawing on the abundance of the MFTA warehouse, and design projects to make your classroom more musical!

*Note: We are excited to announce that we have scholarship funding to waive the MFTA fee for 10 participants. To be eligible, you must be a NYC Public Schools teacher at a Title 1 school, or high ENI school. This opportunity is first-come, first-served. Update: We have reached our limit on scholarships. 

Registration Instructions: If you are taking this course for P-Credits/+30 Credits, you will need to register on both the MFTA and the ASPDP website. Once you register on MFTA, you will receive instructions for registering on ASPDP.

Any questions? Email Will Niedmann at wniedmann@mfta.nyc.gov[/vc_column_text][/vc_column][/vc_row]

events.description:
[vc_row][vc_column][vc_column_text css=””]Course Title: Stop Motion Animation: Storytelling for a Culturally Responsive Classroom

Session 2 — Saturday, November 21st. 9:00 – 5:30 (In-Person)

Session 6 — Saturday, December 19th. 9:00 – 5:30 (Virtual)

Credits: 3 P-Credit/45 CTLE hours*
Fee: $240 (MFTA*)+ $125 (ASPDP)

Course Description: Learn creative animation projects to bring back to your classroom! In this workshop, you will create characters, props, and backgrounds from upcycled materials, building your confidence with reuse practices. Participants will be introduced to a series of art lessons that they then are given time to modify and expand upon for the classroom. You will develop new lessons that use animation as a storytelling medium to support self-expression in your students.

*Note: We are excited to announce that we have scholarship funding to waive the MFTA fee for 10 participants. To be eligible, you must be a NYC Public Schools teacher at a Title 1 school, or high ENI school. This opportunity is first-come, first-served. Update: we have reached our limit on scholarships.

events.title: Film Screening: “Discard Records” by sTo Len
events.description:
[vc_row][vc_column][vc_column_text css=””]Join us on Thursday, November 19, 2026 from 6:30 — 8:30pm for a screening of “Discard Records,” a documentary film by MFTA Artist-in-Residence sTo Len exploring New York City’s waste management systems.

Len began creating the film as he worked as the Public Artist in Residence with the NYC Department of Sanitation, and digitized over 500 hours of the agency’s archival training videos, union films, public service announcements, interviews, environmental programs, cartoons, commercial campaigns, and TV news broadcasts.

This screening of “Discard Records” will include the latest iteration of the film and include addition footage, as he continues to weave together the narrative of New York City’s waste.

Thursday, November 19, 2026 l 6:30 — 8:30pm
At the Materials for the Arts warehouse
33-00 Northern Blvd, 3rd fl.
Long Island City, NY 11101[/vc_column_text][/vc_column][/vc_row]
